intro.title: align-self and justify-self
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple grid layout of colored boxes to practice controlling the placement of individual items within a CSS Grid container. You will learn the core concepts of align-self and justify-self, which allow you to override the default alignment of a single grid item along the block (vertical) and inline (horizontal) axes, respectively. The main technology involved is CSS, specifically using properties like display: grid, align-self, and justify-self. By the end, you'll be able to precisely position items inside a grid independently from the overall container alignment.
intro.usecase: In real-world interfaces, align-self and justify-self are essential for precise control over individual items within grid layouts. Developers use these properties when building dashboards with widgets that need independent positioning, such as a metrics panel where one chart should align differently than others. They're also crucial in forms where specific form fields or buttons require custom alignment within their grid cells, like a submit button that needs to be right-justified while other elements remain centered. These properties give developers fine-grained control to handle edge cases in complex UI components like card layouts, navigation menus, and responsive panels.
